name: The Corner Tower
summary: An octagonal sandstone tower with a machicolated crown and a conical tile roof where the south and west machicolated walls meet.
description: The Burgundian builders turned their corners with octagons: an eight-sided sandstone drum that sees along both walls, crowned like the curtain with a brick frieze and a corbelled parapet over machicolation slots, but roofed against the rain with a steep cone of clay tile. The walks on both walls lead in through doorways in the tower's inner flats; from the outer flats keyhole gun-loops cover the foot of both walls. The roof makes it a landmark and a dry place for the watch; it also makes it the one part of the wall that burns.
build: Cell: 12.1 × 12.1 m (±6.05), no floor slab; walls on the south and west edges, the bailey open to the north-east.

Tower drum: dressed sandstone, octagonal with flats facing the axes, circumradius 2.20 m (apothem 2.03 m), centred (−3.57, −3.57) so its south and west flats lie on the walls' face line 0.45 m in from the cell edge; 0 to 4.60 m.
Tower crown: a brick frieze ring 4.60–5.00 m; two-stage corbels on the five outward flats (S, SW, W, SE, NW), 5.00–5.60 m; a sandstone parapet ring, circumradius 2.60 m, 5.30–6.20 m.
Conical roof: clay tile, eight facets, circumradius 2.65 m at 6.20 m tapering to an iron finial at 8.60 m.
Doorways: soot panels 0.90 × 1.90 m on the tower's north and east flats from 4.00 m, off the walks.

South run: the Late wall section (sandstone 1.60 m, face 0.45 m in, walk 4.00 m, brick frieze, corbels, parapet out to d 0.05, merlons to 5.20 m, timber walk on the inner face) from the tower's south flat corner (x −2.73) to the east cell edge.
West run: the same along the west edge from y −2.73 to the north cell edge.
Keyhole gun-loops: one in each run at 2.10 m along it, and one in each of the tower's south and west flats.
sockets: Wall-walks: 4.00 m, stone plus timber, open at the east and north cell edges
Tower doorways: from both walks into the north and east flats
Keyhole gun-loops: four, on the outer faces
gameplay: The tower is a lookout over both walks; its doorways are the only way from one walk to the other.
The roof is the Late wall's one flammable part.
